box: OTESMALLSERVER (OSS, small server, 2x RTX 5060 Ti, 63.7 GB RAM)
why: Ote: 'record the current commit-pressure situation as an environmental condition, because if the experiment runs later, we need to know that the baseline was healthy enough to make the result meaningful.'
verdict: UNHEALTHY DURING THIS WINDOW. Any contention A/B measured between 18:21 and 18:55 +07 would be uninterpretable: commit swung between 54.8% and 100% of a limit that was itself moving.

outage.message: Windows successfully diagnosed a low virtual memory condition
casualties: postgresql-x64-17 service killed - log ends mid-traffic at 18:21:06 with no shutdown line
VS Code window terminated (reason: oom, code -536870904)
notCasualties: Sotera app :8210 (pid 34664, up since 16:31) - survived, pg pool reconnected on its own
outage.dataIntegrity: clean - on restart: 'database system was not properly shut down' then redo done in 0.01s, no PANIC, no FATAL, no stale postmaster.pid

commitTimeline.note: shortly after the crash, models unloaded
confirmed by a second counter; headroom 0.2 GB
climbed again - the box was oscillating, not settling

residentModelsAtPeak.note: Two of three were CPU-placed. The 35B was correctly on the GPU and STILL contributed ~29 GB of host commit for its mapping - which is the whole reason host commit is now a measured axis.

pagefile.finding: The commit LIMIT is not a constant. Observed at 71.7, 73.2 and 79.7 GB within twenty minutes as the system-managed pagefile grew under pressure and contracted afterwards. Headroom therefore moves for two independent reasons - usage falling AND the limit changing - so any guard that caches the limit will silently misreport.

changesMade: NONE. Ote: 'Leave Ollama, keep-alives, pagefile, and the resident models untouched for now - I don't want environmental changes mixed into the measurement.' No model was stopped, no keep-alive altered, no pagefile resized, ollama never started or killed.

lastDryRun.detail: 54.8% now, but loading the 22.3 GB model would reach 85.9%, above the 85% ceiling
